claims.evidence: All 23 RAW-category files of the PRIDE file list, each used exactly once; every file entry carries projectAccessions PXD001029. The 17 SEARCH zips are not data files.

Each sample-named MaxQuant search (e.g. Baunso_NM_D11103a_main_search) contains exactly two raw files, 20101015_..._COLLAB_Enrico-Parchments_S3x and 20101215_..._Eske_Ancient_Skin_Sample_4x; RAW headers give the same original names for the deposited files mapped to that sample. Table 1 marks samples 1,4,5,6,10,12 with * (procedure A).

Text S1 procedure A: 'For each ancient skin sample, two subsamples ... Each of the two subsamples was processed independently'; Table S2 reports procedure-A spectra as sums of two runs (e.g. 16513+15217). Assignment of subsample 1/2 to the earlier/later run is by acquisition date only.
Each QE search zip contains one raw file whose original name (ANCIENT131-148 with sample name, or B01/B02 for blanks) matches the deposited file name.

claims.value: Capra hircus, Ovis aries, Bos taurus, Caprinae, not applicable (blanks)
claims.evidence: Paper Table 2 'MS' column: goat (samples 1,8,12), cattle (2,10), sheep (3-7,9), sheep/goat (11, Roum -> Caprinae, the narrowest NCBI taxon containing both Ovis and Capra). Modern references: Table 1 domestic sheep CN3213, goat CN3196, cattle. Blanks have no organism.

claims.value: 1-17, one per source (both procedure-A runs of an object share one number)
claims.evidence: Independent skin objects numbered within each species in paper sample-number order, modern reference last; blanks B01=1, B02=2.

claims.value: skin of body (not applicable for blanks)
claims.evidence: Archaeological skin objects (title, Table 1); PRIDE organismParts BTO Skin. For modern references the paper says 'modern comparable material from known species with the same procedure' - skin inferred, see limitations.
No per-sample disease, stage or sex information in paper, supplement or MeSH.
RAW headers: 'LTQ Orbitrap Velos MS' for all 20101015/20101215 files, 'Q Exactive - Orbitrap MS' for all 20120717 files; PRIDE lists both; Text S1 procedure B names the Q Exactive.
Velos method files '150min_Top10HCD_JESPER_Special*.meth'; msms.txt shows Fragmentation=HCD, Mass analyzer=FTMS for Velos (Baunso a) and QE (Karlby b, blank) runs.
Text S1: 'Q Exactive was operated in data-dependent mode ... up to 10 MS/MS'; Velos method name Top10HCD.
Sequencing-grade trypsin (Promega) in both procedures; MaxQuant protease Trypsin/P for every run.

claims.value: Carbamidomethyl C fixed; Oxidation M, Oxidation P, Acetyl K, Deamidated N/Q, Gln->pyro-Glu, Glu->pyro-Glu variable

claims.value: procedure B rows: DTT, chloroacetamide; procedure A rows: not applicable; modern/blank rows: not available
claims.evidence: Text S1 procedure B: lysis buffer with 0.1M DTT, alkylation with 50mM 2-chloroacetamide; procedure A (HCl extraction, trypsin) describes no reduction or alkylation.

claims.value: procedure A / procedure B / not available
claims.evidence: Table 1 footnote: '* Samples prepared following procedure A'; all other archaeological samples procedure B. The procedure used for modern references and blanks is not stated explicitly.
Date prefix of the original acquisition file names recorded in the RAW headers.

limitations: Organism for archaeological samples is the authors' MS-based species assignment (paper Table 2), not an independent a-priori identity; for sample 11 (Roum) the paper could only assign sheep/goat, written as Caprinae.
Organism part 'skin of body' for the three modern reference samples is inferred from 'modern comparable material' and the PRIDE organism part; the tissue is not named explicitly.
Which preparation procedure was used for the modern references and the two blanks is not stated; sample preparation batch, reduction and alkylation reagent are 'not available' on those rows.
Procedure-A subsample identity (subsample 1 vs 2) is not given; technical replicate 1/2 follows acquisition order (Oct 2010 vs Dec 2010).

No per-sample sex, developmental stage or disease information exists; sample 10 (Mogelmose) is reported in the paper as calfskin from foetal haemoglobin peptides, but this was not encoded as a developmental stage.
Archaeological dating, museum numbers and bog locality are carried only in the source names; no ontology-backed SDRF column exists for them.
MaxQuant searched with Trypsin/P; the SDRF records the digestion enzyme as Trypsin.
No factor value column (removed after independent review): species is the result of the study, not a condition; see report.
